candidate: Standard-library data manifest and split fingerprint command (new, inside expctl)
what: A harness command that hashes the full content of configured data paths with sha256, records hub dataset id and commit sha when there are no local files, counts rows per split and class, and writes experiments/data_manifest.json with one root hash.
problem_here: validity.md says every run records a manifest hash but no code builds one; expctl hash leaves out git-ignored data (without git: directories named data or datasets and all non-source file types) and hashes files over 50 MB by size only, so runs on different data can share a provenance hash.
mechanism: Reuse the chunked sha256 loop of hash_files without the size-only shortcut; cache digests by path, size and mtime_ns and say which came from the cache; sorted POSIX relative paths; root hash over the sorted lines; split fingerprint over sorted (split, record hash) pairs.
evidence: Local read of expctl.py lines 107-111, 579-609 and 612-634 and validity.md line 22 at baseline 5ea9659 (2026-11-11, this scout). Content hashes are the stated defence against datasets that change after indexing: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.10149 (2023, paper authors; abstract seen through a search summary).
maturity: Checksum manifests are long-established practice; hashlib ships with every supported Python; no licence issue.
cost: About 100 to 150 lines. Hashing time on very large or network-mounted data was not measured. Text data checked out with different line endings hashes differently on Windows and Linux. A stale cache is possible where mtime is unreliable.
simpler_alternative: Record only sizes and mtimes (misses same-size edits), or keep the current advice-only text.
reason: Closes a verified gap between what the kit claims and what it does; validity is the first-ranked quality attribute; needs no package.
cheap_local_trial: In a temporary test project build a manifest for a small data folder on native Windows and on WSL2, change one byte without changing the size, confirm the root hash changes while source_hash does not, and time a multi-GB file.

candidate: Per-run data hash record and comparison flag (expctl launch and status, runlog)
what: Launch writes the manifest root hash into the run record and exports it to the run (for example as EXP_DATA_HASH); status and comparison output flag runs whose data hashes differ.
problem_here: resume.md and hpo.md refer to a data manifest hash that nothing produces; an unattended loop could keep a result measured on changed data.
mechanism: Same pattern as EXP_SOURCE_HASH and protocol versions: record at launch, compare at decision time, warn or refuse on mismatch.
evidence: Local read of runlog.py, resume.md line 11 and hpo.md line 52 at baseline 5ea9659 (2026-11-11, this scout). No external measurement; the rationale is the leakage taxonomy at https://reproducible.cs.princeton.edu/ (table updated May 2024, Kapoor and Narayanan).
maturity: Kit-internal practice; mirrors what experiment trackers do with dataset versions.
cost: Small change in three files. What the unattended loop does on a mismatch (stop, or open a new protocol version) must be designed.
simpler_alternative: Write the hash into the journal by hand, which is the current advice-only state.
reason: Without it the manifest has no effect on what the loop keeps.
cheap_local_trial: Launch two dummy runs on different data folders in a temporary test project and check that status shows two data hashes and flags the comparison.

candidate: Harness-run cross-split exact-duplicate audit that prints counts only
what: An expctl subcommand that hashes normalised records of every split, sealed ones included, and prints collision counts per pair of splits.
problem_here: validity.md section 2 asks the agent to hash-compare splits, but section 5 and the guard deny it the sealed test set; duplicates across splits inflate scores.
mechanism: sha256 of a stated canonical form (text: Unicode NFKC, casefold, collapsed whitespace; files: content hash); set intersection; output is counts. Listing the colliding training rows is a separate, logged step.
evidence: CIFAR-100: 10 percent of test images have duplicates or near-duplicates in train, error 2.9 percent on those against 26.1 overall: https://www.mdpi.com/2313-433X/6/6/41 (2 Jun 2020, paper authors). Language-model corpora: over 4 percent of validation affected: https://aclanthology.org/2022.acl-long.577/ (May 2022, paper authors). Visual datasets: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.17416 (24 Aug 2025, paper authors).
maturity: Standard practice since the duplicate-free CIFAR test sets of 2020; standard library only for exact matches.
cost: Needs a record reader per format (JSONL, CSV, text and image files work with the standard library; Parquet and Arrow need the repository loader or an optional module). Exact matching is a lower bound on near-duplicates. The output is a small oracle about test membership. The guard must allow this command and nothing else on sealed paths.
simpler_alternative: Leave the check to the user outside the agent session.
reason: The only way to run a required validity check without unsealing the test set.
cheap_local_trial: Make toy JSONL train and test sets with 5 planted duplicates, seal the test path, confirm the agent cannot read it and the command prints 5.

candidate: Deterministic hash-bucket group split (standard-library snippet in the references)
what: Assign each group id (user, patient, document, site) to a split by sha256(salt + group id) modulo N.
problem_here: validity.md names group leakage but the kit offers no dependency-free way to make a group split that stays stable when data grows.
mechanism: Stable hash of the unit of independence; the salt goes into the manifest; no shuffling state to lose.
evidence: Dependent train and test samples are one of eight leakage types in a survey covering 648 affected papers: https://reproducible.cs.princeton.edu/ (updated May 2024, Kapoor and Narayanan). Identity overlap biases face-recognition accuracy upward: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09403 (2024, paper authors). The snippet itself was not measured (Inferred).
maturity: Long-standing practice for stable splits; standard library only.
cost: About ten lines of advice. Split sizes are approximate and there is no stratification.
simpler_alternative: scikit-learn group splitters when scikit-learn is installed.
reason: Gives the core route against the most damaging non-duplicate leakage at no dependency cost.
cheap_local_trial: Split 10,000 synthetic group ids, add 1,000 more, confirm no existing id changes split and no group spans two splits.

candidate: Data-record fields in the journal Project card (source and revision, licence and where read, terms, personal data, synthetic share, dedup, split salt)
what: Replace the single free-text Data line of templates/JOURNAL.md with a short checklist that the agent fills in Phase 0.
problem_here: Licence source, dataset revision, terms acceptance, personal data, synthetic share and deduplication settings are never recorded.
mechanism: A twelve-item checklist (listed in the note under Q4) in which the values unknown and unspecified are allowed and visible.
evidence: Licence unspecified for about 70 percent of 1,858 audited datasets and the hub label more permissive than the source for 27 percent on the largest hub: https://www.nature.com/articles/s42256-024-00878-8 (2024, Data Provenance Initiative).
maturity: Datasheets and data cards are established practice; the audit is peer reviewed.
cost: A few more lines for the agent to read and fill; risk of box-ticking with unknown everywhere.
simpler_alternative: Keep one free-text line.
reason: Cheap, and the unattended loop needs these facts written down before it starts.
cheap_local_trial: Fill the card by hand for one public dataset and time it.

candidate: Rule: the agent never accepts dataset or model terms; it stops and asks the user
what: A line in the skill, and a guard pattern if feasible, that gated-access acceptance and licence click-through are user actions.
problem_here: An unattended agent with a hub token could request access to gated data or models on the user's behalf.
mechanism: Instruction text; the hub lookup records the gated flag; the loop treats a gated repository without recorded user acceptance as a stop condition.
evidence: The hub API exposes gated as false, auto or manual: https://github.com/huggingface/hub-docs/blob/8577fc77/docs/hub/api.md (official docs). Custom model licences carry duties such as naming rules: https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3_1/LICENSE (23 Jul 2024).
maturity: Policy practice; no tooling needed.
cost: One line of text; an unattended run stops when it meets a gated source.
simpler_alternative: None simpler.
reason: Accepting terms binds the user; the kit must not let the agent do it.
cheap_local_trial: Ask the agent in a test project to load a gated dataset and observe whether it stops and asks.

candidate: Dataset-file safety rule: prefer Parquet, Arrow, JSONL and CSV; treat pickle-backed files and loader scripts as code
what: A dated rule in the references, and optionally a guard pattern, that data files which execute code on load need the same approval as running code.
problem_here: The kit says nothing about dataset files as executable content; an agent told to try a dataset can trigger code execution.
mechanism: Name the risky forms (pickle and joblib files, loader scripts, remote-code flags); the agent asks before loading them; optional guard pattern on remote-code flags.
evidence: CVE-2026-57845, CVSS 4.0 score 8.7, datasets up to 5.1.0: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-57845 (published 23 Oct 2026, NVD). Loading scripts were removed in datasets 4.0.0 (9 Jul 2025): https://github.com/huggingface/datasets/releases.
maturity: Well-known class of flaw; Parquet and safetensors are the usual safe formats.
cost: Advice plus perhaps one guard pattern; an incomplete list gives false comfort.
simpler_alternative: Rely on library defaults.
reason: Direct evidence of a current exploit path in the most common loader; unattended safety is the third-ranked attribute.
cheap_local_trial: none (do not run an exploit); check a guard pattern against a harmless command line that contains a remote-code flag.

candidate: Dated advisory for datasets below 5.2.0 (reference text plus a warning in expctl env)
what: expctl env already prints the installed datasets version; add a dated note that versions up to 5.1.0 have a pickle code-execution flaw fixed in 5.2.0.
problem_here: The flaw was published on the day the kit was built and nothing in the kit flags it.
mechanism: A small dated advisory table keyed by package and fixed version; env prints a warning when the installed version is lower.
evidence: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-57845 (23 Oct 2026, NVD); fix https://github.com/huggingface/datasets/pull/8879 (merged 9 Nov 2026); https://github.com/huggingface/datasets/releases/tag/5.2.0 (9 Nov 2026).
maturity: datasets: Apache-2.0, about 22,100 stars, 5.2.0 released 9 Nov 2026.
cost: A static table goes stale; it needs a date and a refresh path (the scouting step). Whether 5.2.0 closes every pickle path was not checked.
simpler_alternative: Mention it once in the release notes of the kit.
reason: Cheap, current and specific; shows the pattern for dated advice.
cheap_local_trial: Run expctl env in a temporary test project with datasets 5.1.0 in a clean virtual environment and check the warning text (not run by this scout).

candidate: Untrusted-row rule: dataset rows, cards and READMEs are data, not instructions; inspect samples through bounded harness output
what: A rule in the skill that text inside datasets is never followed, plus sample inspection through a command that truncates rows and limits their number.
problem_here: The kit tells the agent to inspect about 50 items; rows are attacker-controllable text, and every row the agent reads is sent to the model provider.
mechanism: Instruction-source boundary stated in SKILL.md; a sample viewer prints a bounded number of truncated rows; the user decides in the Project card whether raw rows may be shown at all.
evidence: No study found on dataset rows read by a coding agent. Adjacent: a survey of prompt injection against coding agents, https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17548 (2026; seen through a search summary only, Inferred).
maturity: Indirect prompt injection is a documented class with no settled defence.
cost: A few lines of text; a rule does not stop a successful injection; a viewer adds code.
simpler_alternative: Rely on the agent product's own defences.
reason: The brief forbids acting on instructions in fetched content; dataset text is the same class of input.
cheap_local_trial: Plant a row that asks for a sealed path to be printed in a toy dataset, ask the agent to inspect samples in a temporary project, and observe whether it obeys.

candidate: Deduplication policy: required across splits, a tested hypothesis inside the training set, with tool version and parameters recorded
what: Reference text that separates the validity requirement (no duplicates across splits) from the optimisation choice (deduplicating training data), and asks for method, tool version, threshold and counts in the manifest.
problem_here: validity.md treats deduplication as one item with no warning about over-deduplication or about results that change with tool version.
mechanism: Two rules and four recorded fields; within-train deduplication is run as an experiment against a baseline.
evidence: Global MinHash deduplication over 96 crawl snapshots gave little gain and lighter global variants were worse: https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/370df50ccfdf8bde18f8f9c2d9151bda-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf (2024, dataset authors). Deduplicated models emit memorised text about ten times less often: https://aclanthology.org/2022.acl-long.577/ (2022, paper authors). The default hash scheme changed in datasketch 2.0.0: https://github.com/ekzhu/datasketch/releases (5 Jul 2026).
maturity: Peer-reviewed evidence on both sides; no tooling needed for the rule.
cost: Text only; the nuance may be skipped by an agent in a hurry.
simpler_alternative: Keep the single line in validity.md.
reason: Prevents both leakage and the opposite error of deleting useful data on undated advice.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Standard-library regex tripwire for secrets and obvious personal data, counts only
what: A small scan for about a dozen high-precision patterns (private-key headers, common key prefixes, email addresses, phone-like strings) that reports counts by category and never prints the matches.
problem_here: The kit has no personal-data or secrets step, and fine-tuned models memorise such strings.
mechanism: The re module over text records of the training split; counts by pattern; the result goes into the Project card with the pattern-set date.
evidence: 11,908 live secrets in one web-crawl snapshot: https://trufflesecurity.com/blog/research-finds-12-000-live-api-keys-and-passwords-in-deepseek-s-training-data (27 Feb 2025, scanner vendor). Regular-expression recognisers carried the best result on one detector benchmark: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15776 (17 Apr 2026, single author).
maturity: Regex scanning is the base of every secrets scanner; pattern sets age.
cost: About 60 lines; low recall; false positives; a clean result may be over-trusted; the pattern list needs a date.
simpler_alternative: Ask the user whether the data holds personal data or secrets and record the answer.
reason: A cheap tripwire with direct evidence of the problem; its recall must be stated as low.
cheap_local_trial: Run the patterns over a public text sample with 20 planted fake keys and email addresses; count hits and false positives.

candidate: Per-example loss ranking for label review (standard library, from run logs)
what: The run writes per-example loss or margin at a few checkpoints; a helper ranks training items for human or agent review.
problem_here: validity.md asks for a 50-item inspection but gives no way to choose items likely to be wrong.
mechanism: Training-dynamics signal as a ranking; review before any removal; flagged items are never deleted automatically.
evidence: Ten test sets average at least 3.3 percent label errors, and 51 percent of algorithmic flags were confirmed by people: https://datasets-benchmarks-proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/file/f2217062e9a397a1dca429e7d70bc6ca-Paper-round1.pdf (2021, paper authors). Margin and confidence dynamics identify mislabelled items: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.10528 (v4 23 Dec 2020) and https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.10795 (v2 15 Oct 2020), paper authors. That a plain loss ranking does as well was not measured (Inferred).
maturity: Methods date from 2020 and are widely cited; no package needed.
cost: Run-side logging of per-example values and their storage; showing rows to the agent sends them to the provider; high loss also marks hard but correct items.
simpler_alternative: Random 50-item inspection, as today.
reason: Plausible gain at low cost; the exact form needs a local check first.
cheap_local_trial: Train a small classifier on CIFAR-10 with 5 percent flipped labels on the RTX 5090 for a few minutes and measure what share of the 500 highest-loss items are flipped.

candidate: Standard-library n-gram overlap check between training text and evaluation sets
what: Count evaluation items that share a long token n-gram with the training or fine-tuning text; the n-gram length is recorded.
problem_here: finetuning.md has one line asking for an overlap check and gives no method; validity.md names n-gram overlap without a tool.
mechanism: Hash whitespace-token n-grams of the evaluation set into a set, stream the training text, count evaluation items hit; run by the harness for sealed sets, counts only.
evidence: Train-test overlap affects over 4 percent of standard language-model validation sets: https://aclanthology.org/2022.acl-long.577/ (May 2022, paper authors). No settled n-gram length was found (Inferred).
maturity: Used in large-model evaluation reports for years; standard library only.
cost: Memory grows with the evaluation set; whitespace tokens differ from model tokens; cannot inspect a pretrained model's own corpus.
simpler_alternative: The exact-duplicate audit alone.
reason: Extends the exact audit to partial copies; needs a threshold trial before any number is written down.
cheap_local_trial: Plant 10 evaluation passages inside a 100 MB text file and check the count and the run time.

candidate: Synthetic-data provenance rule: per-row tag, generation from the training split only, generator and terms recorded
what: A rule that each synthetic row carries a flag, generator id, prompt hash and seed row ids, and that generation never reads validation or test rows.
problem_here: validity.md mentions synthetic samples in one clause; nothing records the share, the generator or its terms.
mechanism: Tag at creation and keep it through transformations; the manifest records the synthetic share; the cross-split duplicate audit also covers synthetic rows.
evidence: Provider terms bar training competing models on outputs: https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ (effective 1 Jan 2026) and https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms (effective 17 Jun 2025). Synthetic fine-tuning caused forgetting on real data: https://aclanthology.org/2026.emnlp-industry.172/ (2026, paper authors).
maturity: Practice; no tooling needed.
cost: A few lines of advice and two manifest fields; tags are lost when a pipeline drops columns.
simpler_alternative: Record only a dataset-level synthetic share.
reason: Needed to keep evaluation data clean and to answer licence questions later.
cheap_local_trial: Generate 20 rows with any local model, tag them, merge and shuffle them with real rows, and confirm the manifest reports the share.

candidate: Synthetic mixing hypothesis: add to real data, never replace it; compare against a real-only baseline at equal budget
what: A dated technique entry for the references.
problem_here: An unattended agent may propose synthetic data as an easy gain; the kit has no guidance on when it harms.
mechanism: Accumulation keeps the real-data signal; replacement compounds generator errors.
evidence: Replacing real data leads to collapse while accumulating keeps test loss bounded; in fine-tuning a 2B model synthetic data helped only with about 1,024 or fewer real examples: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/kazdan25a.html (ICML 2025, paper authors). Fine-tuning on synthetic rationales hurt: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10279 (2026, paper authors).
maturity: Peer-reviewed results from 2024 to 2026; thresholds are task-specific.
cost: Text only; a share threshold may be read as a default.
simpler_alternative: Say nothing and let each experiment decide.
reason: A dated, sourced hypothesis that heads off a known harmful pattern.
cheap_local_trial: Fine-tune a small model on 1k real rows with and without 1k synthetic rows at equal steps, three seeds, on the RTX 5090.

candidate: Order the kit's leakage checks by measured effect (selection, then duplicates and groups, then learned preprocessing, then normalisation)
what: Reorder and annotate validity.md section 2 so that the agent spends effort where leakage is largest.
problem_here: The checklist is flat; an agent may spend effort on scaler statistics and skip the duplicate audit.
mechanism: Ordering plus one dated sentence per item on measured effect size.
evidence: Across 2,047 tabular datasets normalisation leakage changed AUC by at most 0.005, selection leakage was largest and the duplication effect grew with model capacity: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.04199 (v2 29 May 2026, single author). Feature selection before the split gives 0.76 accuracy on random data: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html (version 1.9.1, project docs).
maturity: One large single-author study, tabular data only.
cost: Text change; risk of under-weighting normalisation leakage for neural networks, where it was not measured.
simpler_alternative: Keep the flat list.
reason: Promising, but the main evidence is tabular and from one author; enter as a hypothesis.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Hub metadata lookup module: commit sha, licence fields and gating through the hub REST API with urllib
what: An optional command that fetches a dataset or model record and writes sha, licence, licence link, gated flag and tags into the manifest.
problem_here: Datasets loaded by name drift between runs; licence and gating are never recorded.
mechanism: GET https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/{repo_id} or the same path with /revision/{revision}; read sha, card licence fields, gated, tags and the file list.
evidence: Endpoints: https://github.com/huggingface/hub-docs/blob/8577fc77/docs/hub/api.md (official docs). Revision pinning: https://github.com/huggingface/datasets/blob/main/docs/source/loading.mdx (datasets 5.2.0). Labels are unreliable: https://www.nature.com/articles/s42256-024-00878-8 (2024).
maturity: Public API in long use; field stability was not checked.
cost: A network call, so off by default; a token is needed for gated or private repositories; the repository id leaves the machine; the label may be wrong.
simpler_alternative: Ask the user to paste the commit sha and the licence.
reason: Makes the revision pin and the licence record cheap; needs the network.
cheap_local_trial: Fetch one public dataset record with a three-line urllib script and read sha, gated and licence.

what: A CLI command that checks cached or local files of a repository revision against hub checksums and exits non-zero on mismatch.
problem_here: A hub revision pin trusts the local cache; nothing confirms that local bytes match.
mechanism: hf cache verify REPO_ID --repo-type dataset --revision <sha> --fail-on-missing-files --fail-on-extra-files
evidence: https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/blob/v2.4.0/docs/source/en/package_reference/cli.md (v2.4.0, 29 Oct 2026, official docs).
maturity: huggingface_hub 2.4.0 released 29 Oct 2026; very widely used client library.
cost: Needs the package and the network; a token for gated repositories.
simpler_alternative: The standard-library manifest hashes local files without the network.
reason: A useful closing check for hub data, only where the package is already installed.
cheap_local_trial: In a clean virtual environment verify one small public dataset, then alter one cached file and run it again.

candidate: Hugging Face dataset viewer REST API
what: Hosted endpoints for split names, sizes, column statistics, Parquet file lists and Croissant metadata.
problem_here: Row counts and split names for the manifest without a download.
mechanism: GET https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/splits, /size, /statistics, /parquet or /croissant with a dataset parameter; rows endpoints return at most 100 rows per call.
evidence: https://huggingface.co/docs/dataset-viewer/quick_start (official docs).
maturity: Hosted service; not every dataset is valid for it.
cost: Network service; bearer token for gated or private data; the rows endpoints bring dataset text into the agent context; rate limits not checked.
simpler_alternative: The hub REST record plus local counts.
reason: Convenient, but a service dependency for facts the manifest can compute locally.
cheap_local_trial: Fetch /splits and /size for one public dataset with urllib.

what: An MLCommons JSON-LD format that describes dataset files, record sets and licence.
problem_here: none found beyond what the kit's own manifest does; a possible export format.
mechanism: Read the hub-served Croissant record and map licence and file entries into the manifest.
evidence: https://github.com/mlcommons/croissant (v1.1.1, 5 Oct 2026, GitHub API). No evidence found that it improves training validity.
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 920 stars; 1.1.1 released 5 Oct 2026.
cost: Reading JSON-LD needs only the standard library; the reference package is a further dependency; coverage of hashes in hub-served records was not checked.
simpler_alternative: The kit's own flat JSON manifest.
reason: No use found today; watch as an interchange format.
cheap_local_trial: Fetch the Croissant record of one public dataset and list which manifest fields it fills.

what: Data versioning beside git: small pointer files in git, content in a cache or remote store.
problem_here: Repositories that already use it hold data identity in dvc.lock and .dvc files; the kit should recognise that instead of duplicating it.
mechanism: Pointer files are tracked text, so the existing source hash already covers them; the kit asks for a clean dvc status before a run.
evidence: https://dvc.org/blog/dvc-joins-lakefs-your-questions-answered/ (acquired 18 Nov 2025, vendor). Release 3.67.1 on 31 Mar 2026 and last commit 6 Nov 2026 (GitHub API, treeverse/dvc). No measured effect on training results found.
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 16,000 stars; active; owner changed in Nov 2025.
cost: A package with many dependencies; ownership change; a second source of truth if the kit also writes a manifest.
simpler_alternative: The standard-library manifest.
reason: Do not add it; detect it and reuse its pointer files where it is already present.
cheap_local_trial: In a temporary git project with one DVC-tracked file, check that expctl hash changes when the pointer file changes (needs DVC in a throwaway environment).

what: A server that gives git-like branches and commits over object storage.
problem_here: none found for a single-node kit.
mechanism: A running server in front of an object store; clients read through it.
evidence: https://lakefs.io/blog/lakefs-business-source-license/ (22 Sep 2026, vendor): community edition under the Business Source License from 1.87.0. Release 1.88.0 on 1 Oct 2026 (GitHub API, treeverse/lakeFS).
maturity: About 5,600 stars; licence changed from open source to source-available in Sep 2026.
cost: A server to run; source-available licence; far beyond the kit's scale.
simpler_alternative: The standard-library manifest, or DVC where already used.
reason: Needs a service and no longer has an open-source licence; no use here.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: A data version-control CLI and library built for large datasets.
problem_here: none found beyond what the manifest gives.
mechanism: Content-addressed commits of data files with its own remote protocol.
evidence: https://github.com/Oxen-AI/Oxen (v0.67.1, 10 Nov 2026, GitHub API). No independent evidence found.
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 1,200 stars; active; Windows binaries published.
cost: A binary or package to install; small user base; a second source of truth.
simpler_alternative: The standard-library manifest.
reason: Active and Windows-friendly, but small adoption and no need shown.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: A Python library for typed, versioned datasets over cloud object stores.
problem_here: none found.
mechanism: A metadata layer over files in cloud object storage.
evidence: https://github.com/datachain-ai/datachain (v0.62.4, 9 Nov 2026, GitHub API). No evidence on training results found.
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 2,800 stars; active; repositioned toward cloud data layers.
cost: A package and cloud storage; positioning has shifted.
simpler_alternative: The standard-library manifest.
reason: Aimed at cloud data lakes, not at a single-node training kit.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: An in-process SQL engine that reads Parquet, CSV and JSON files directly.
problem_here: Row-level cross-split checks on Parquet data need a reader the standard library lacks.
mechanism: A SQL intersect or anti-join on a hash of normalised columns, read straight from the split files.
evidence: https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb (v2.0.0, 21 Oct 2026, GitHub API). No measurement for this use.
maturity: MIT; about 43,000 stars; very active.
cost: One binary package; its hash and normalisation functions differ from the standard-library path, so counts must come from one path only.
simpler_alternative: Have the repository's own loader write record hashes to a text file for the core audit.
reason: The lightest way to reach Parquet rows; only needed when the repository cannot emit record hashes.
cheap_local_trial: Install in a throwaway environment and run a cross-split intersect on two small Parquet files.

what: A library that flags likely label errors with confident learning.
problem_here: Choosing which training or validation items to review for label errors.
mechanism: Out-of-sample predicted probabilities compared with given labels; ranked candidates.
evidence: 51 percent of flagged items were confirmed as errors by people, and ten test sets averaged at least 3.3 percent errors: https://datasets-benchmarks-proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/file/f2217062e9a397a1dca429e7d70bc6ca-Paper-round1.pdf (2021, the method's authors). Repository state: https://github.com/cleanlab/cleanlab (v2.9.0 on 13 Jan 2026, no later commit; GitHub API) and https://cleanlab.ai/blog/handshake-acquires-cleanlab/ (28 Jan 2026).
maturity: Repository created 2018; Apache-2.0 after a change from AGPL-3.0; about 11,700 stars; dormant for ten months after an acquisition.
cost: Needs cross-validated probabilities (extra training); NumPy and scikit-learn dependencies; risk of breaking with newer NumPy or Python while unmaintained; half the flags are wrong.
simpler_alternative: Per-example loss ranking from run logs.
reason: The best-evidenced label-error method, but upstream is dormant; pin if used and never auto-delete.
cheap_local_trial: CIFAR-10 with 5 percent flipped labels and out-of-fold probabilities from a small network; compare flag precision with loss ranking.

what: MinHash and locality-sensitive hashing building blocks for near-duplicate search.
problem_here: Near-duplicates across splits and inside training text that exact hashing misses.
mechanism: MinHash signatures over word n-grams and an LSH index queried at a Jaccard threshold.
evidence: MinHash settings with ablations in a large web corpus (word 5-grams, 112 hashes, 14 buckets of 8): https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/370df50ccfdf8bde18f8f9c2d9151bda-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf (2024, dataset authors, who used another library). Release notes: https://github.com/ekzhu/datasketch/releases (v2.0.0, 5 Jul 2026).
maturity: Repository created 2015; MIT; about 3,000 stars; last push 26 Oct 2026.
cost: NumPy dependency; 2.0.0 changed the default hash scheme, so sketches differ from 1.x unless the legacy scheme is set; threshold choice; memory on large corpora.
simpler_alternative: The exact-duplicate audit on normalised text.
reason: The smallest maintained dependency for near-duplicate text; version and parameters must be recorded.
cheap_local_trial: In a throwaway environment sketch 100k short documents with 5 percent planted near-duplicates; measure recall at Jaccard 0.75 and the time taken.

what: Embedding-based deduplication within one set or across two sets.
problem_here: Paraphrase-level duplicates between training and evaluation text.
mechanism: Embeddings and approximate nearest-neighbour search with a similarity threshold.
evidence: https://github.com/MinishLab/semhash (v0.5.0, 30 Sep 2026, GitHub API). No independent measurement found.
maturity: Repository created Oct 2024; MIT; about 980 stars.
cost: Needs an embedding model, probably downloaded on first use (recalled, not re-read); semantic matches need review; young project.
simpler_alternative: datasketch, or the exact audit.
reason: Covers a real gap (paraphrases) but has no independent evidence yet.
cheap_local_trial: In a throwaway environment run 10k training rows against 1k test rows with planted paraphrases.

what: A collection of text deduplication scripts (MinHash, SimHash, suffix array, exact).
problem_here: Same as datasketch.
mechanism: Batch scripts over datasets.
evidence: https://github.com/ChenghaoMou/text-dedup (last release 2023.09.20, last push 9 Mar 2026, GitHub API).
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 770 stars; no release for three years.
cost: Stale releases; extra dependencies.
simpler_alternative: datasketch.
reason: No release since 2023; another candidate covers the need.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Semantic deduplication of the training set (embedding clusters, keep one item per cluster)
what: Remove training items whose embeddings are near-identical to others.
problem_here: Possible training-cost saving on redundant data; none shown for this kit.
mechanism: Embed, cluster, drop all but one item per tight cluster.
evidence: Half of a large image-text subset removed with minimal loss: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09540 (2023, paper authors; abstract seen through a search summary, Inferred). Counter-evidence that more deduplication is not always better: https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/370df50ccfdf8bde18f8f9c2d9151bda-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf (2024, dataset authors).
maturity: Research technique from 2023; results depend on data and threshold.
cost: Embedding compute; over-deduplication risk; one more tuned threshold.
simpler_alternative: Exact and MinHash deduplication.
reason: A hypothesis to test per dataset, never a default.
cheap_local_trial: Embed 50k rows with a small local model on the RTX 5090, drop near-identical items at cosine 0.95, and compare a short fine-tune with and without them.

what: A GPU-accelerated curation toolkit for large text, image and video corpora.
problem_here: none found at single-node fine-tuning scale; relevant for pretraining-size corpora.
mechanism: Distributed pipelines with deduplication and quality filters.
evidence: Install requirements: https://docs.nvidia.com/nemo/curator/latest/admin/installation.html (docs labelled v1.4.0, 26.09; vendor docs). Release 1.4.0 on 9 Oct 2026 (GitHub API, NVIDIA-NeMo/Curator). No independent result evidence found.
maturity: Repository created Mar 2024; Apache-2.0; about 1,900 stars; active.
cost: Docs recommend Ubuntu and do not mention Windows or WSL2; GPU extras are built for CUDA 12 while the test machine has a CUDA 13 PyTorch; heavy dependency set.
simpler_alternative: datasketch or datatrove.
reason: Pays off only at corpus scale, and platform support for this machine is unknown.
cheap_local_trial: none on native Windows; on WSL2 a CPU-only install in a throwaway environment would show whether it installs at all.

what: A large operator library for cleaning, filtering, deduplicating and redacting text and multimodal data.
problem_here: A ready set of filters for instruction and pretraining text; no specific gap shown.
mechanism: Recipes of mapper, filter and deduplicator operators; includes a personal-data redaction mapper.
evidence: https://github.com/datajuicer/data-juicer (v1.6.2, 4 Nov 2026, GitHub API and release notes). Result claims come from its authors; no independent comparison found.
maturity: Repository created Aug 2023; Apache-2.0; about 7,200 stars; active.
cost: Large dependency tree; operator defaults are undated advice; recipes add a second configuration language.
simpler_alternative: A few standard-library filters plus datasketch.
reason: Broad and active, but no independent evidence of result gains; a candidate for a pinned optional recipe.
cheap_local_trial: Install in a throwaway WSL2 environment and run a three-operator recipe on a 10k-row JSONL file.

what: A pipeline library for filtering and deduplicating web-scale text.
problem_here: Relevant only when a user builds pretraining text corpora.
mechanism: Readers, filters, MinHash and exact deduplication blocks run locally or on a cluster.
evidence: The corpus built with it reports ablations for each filtering and deduplication step: https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/370df50ccfdf8bde18f8f9c2d9151bda-Paper-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.pdf (2024, the library's authors). Release 0.10.1 on 30 Sep 2026 (GitHub API, huggingface/datatrove).
maturity: Repository created Jun 2023; Apache-2.0; about 3,400 stars; active.
cost: Built for crawl-scale data; too heavy for small fine-tuning sets.
simpler_alternative: datasketch.
reason: Has the best published ablations among the pipeline tools; narrow use.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: A system of model-driven operators and pipelines for data preparation and synthesis.
problem_here: none found.
mechanism: Operator pipelines that call language models to clean, score and generate data.
evidence: https://github.com/OpenDCAI/DataFlow (v1.0.13, 26 Oct 2026, GitHub API and release note). Claims come from its authors only.
maturity: Repository created Oct 2024; Apache-2.0; about 8,500 stars; active.
cost: The release note pins pandas 2.3.3 for NumPy 1.26.4, which is likely to conflict with a NumPy 2 training environment; many operators need model API access.
simpler_alternative: A short script, or a lighter generation toolkit.
reason: Environment-conflict risk breaks the rule not to disturb the user's environment; no independent evidence.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: Perceptual-hash and CNN-embedding duplicate finder for images.
problem_here: Near-duplicate images across splits, which file hashes miss.
mechanism: Perceptual hashes compared by Hamming distance, or embeddings compared by cosine similarity.
evidence: The problem is measured in https://www.mdpi.com/2313-433X/6/6/41 (2020) and https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.17416 (2025) by other authors; the tool itself was not benchmarked there. Repository: https://github.com/idealo/imagededup (v0.3.3.post2, 15 Aug 2025, GitHub API).
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 5,700 stars; no push since Aug 2025.
cost: Image and deep-learning dependencies; fifteen months without commits; thresholds need tuning per dataset.
simpler_alternative: File hashes for exact duplicates.
reason: Fills the image near-duplicate gap, but maintenance has stopped for now.
cheap_local_trial: In a throwaway environment run its perceptual-hash finder on CIFAR-100 train against test and compare with the published 10 percent.

what: A fast duplicate, outlier and label-issue finder for image and video datasets.
problem_here: Same as imagededup.
mechanism: Embeddings and nearest-neighbour graphs.
evidence: https://github.com/visual-layer/fastdup (GitHub API: licence reported as Other, last push 23 Aug 2026).
maturity: About 1,900 stars; non-standard licence.
cost: The licence is not a standard open-source one, so terms would need review for every user; the core is reported to be closed (recalled, not re-checked).
simpler_alternative: imagededup, or file hashes.
reason: A kit module should not depend on a tool with a non-standard licence.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: A suite of data and model validation checks, including train-test leakage checks.
problem_here: Overlaps with the kit's own leakage checks.
mechanism: Prebuilt check suites over dataframes and vision datasets.
evidence: https://github.com/deepchecks/deepchecks (v0.19.1, 15 Dec 2024; last push 28 Dec 2025; licence reported as Other; GitHub API).
maturity: About 4,100 stars; no release for almost two years.
cost: Stale; non-standard licence label; heavy dependencies.
simpler_alternative: The core audits.
reason: Stale and replaceable by small core checks.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: Schema validation for dataframes.
problem_here: none found (schema drift is not a gap this kit has evidence for).
mechanism: Declared column types and checks validated at load time.
evidence: https://github.com/unionai-oss/pandera (v0.36.0, 10 Nov 2026, GitHub API). No evidence on training results found.
maturity: MIT; about 4,500 stars; active.
cost: A package and schema upkeep.
simpler_alternative: Counts per split and class in the manifest.
reason: Healthy project but no problem here for it to solve.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: scikit-learn 1.9.1 group and time splitters and Pipeline (as dated advice)
what: Keep the existing advice to use GroupKFold, StratifiedGroupKFold, time-based splits and to fit preprocessing inside a Pipeline, with version and date added.
problem_here: validity.md names these tools without version or date; they are the optional route beside the hash-bucket split.
mechanism: Splitters keep groups together; Pipeline fits transforms on the training folds only.
evidence: On random data, feature selection before the split gives 0.76 accuracy against 0.5 when fitted on the training set only: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html (version 1.9.1, 11 Sep 2026, project docs).
maturity: Mature and very widely used library.
cost: A package dependency, often already present.
simpler_alternative: The hash-bucket group split.
reason: Already in the kit as advice; only the date and source are missing.
cheap_local_trial: Reproduce the random-data example from the docs in two minutes where scikit-learn is installed.

what: A personal-data detection and anonymisation framework (regular expressions plus named-entity models).
problem_here: An optional scan of training text for personal data before fine-tuning.
mechanism: Recognisers per entity type; the analyser returns spans; the anonymiser replaces them.
evidence: Best of eight systems on one benchmark at span F1 0.1385: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15776 (17 Apr 2026, single author). Release: https://github.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio (2.2.366, 27 Oct 2026, GitHub API).
maturity: MIT; about 11,800 stars; repository moved organisation; Python 3.11 to 3.14.
cost: Needs a language-model download; low measured recall; slow on large corpora; replaced text can damage training data.
simpler_alternative: The regex tripwire.
reason: The most used detector, yet independent recall is low; offer only as a pinned scan with counts-only output.
cheap_local_trial: In a throwaway environment scan 1k synthetic rows with planted names, email addresses and phone numbers and report recall.

what: Small zero-shot entity models, several fine-tuned for personal-data labels.
problem_here: Same as Presidio, with better measured span accuracy.
mechanism: A span-classification encoder prompted with label names.
evidence: Five detectors scored 0.368 to 0.471 exact-span F1, the best being a model of this family: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09973 (2026, paper authors). Library: https://github.com/urchade/GLiNER (v0.2.30, 2 Nov 2026, GitHub API).
maturity: Apache-2.0 library; about 4,200 stars; model checkpoints carry their own licences.
cost: Model download; a GPU helps; recall below one half on that benchmark; the licence of each checkpoint must be read.
simpler_alternative: The regex tripwire.
reason: Best measured open option, still a tripwire and not a guarantee.
cheap_local_trial: Run one checkpoint on the RTX 5090 over 1k planted rows and compare with Presidio.

what: A token-classification model for eight personal-data categories, including secrets.
problem_here: Same as Presidio.
mechanism: A 1.5B-parameter model with a 128,000-token context that labels spans.
evidence: Model card: https://huggingface.co/openai/privacy-filter (Apache-2.0; the card says it gives no anonymisation or compliance guarantee). Independent exact-span F1 0.373: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09973 (2026, paper authors).
maturity: Released in 2026 (exact date from secondary sources, Unverified); Apache-2.0.
cost: Large download; GPU time; fixed categories; modest independent accuracy.
simpler_alternative: The regex tripwire.
reason: Open and long-context, but independent accuracy is modest.
cheap_local_trial: Load it on the RTX 5090 in a throwaway environment and scan 1k planted rows.

what: A secrets scanner with many detectors and optional live verification.
problem_here: An optional deeper scan of training text and repositories for credentials.
mechanism: Pattern detectors over files; optional calls to providers to test whether a found credential is live.
evidence: The vendor found 11,908 live secrets in one web-crawl snapshot: https://trufflesecurity.com/blog/research-finds-12-000-live-api-keys-and-passwords-in-deepseek-s-training-data (27 Feb 2025, vendor measured). Release 3.99.8 on 2 Nov 2026 (GitHub API, trufflesecurity/trufflehog).
maturity: AGPL-3.0; about 29,200 stars; very active.
cost: AGPL binary, so run it as an external tool and never bundle it; live verification sends found credentials over the network and must stay off; binary download; flag names were not checked.
simpler_alternative: The regex tripwire, or gitleaks.
reason: Strongest detector set, but licence and network verification need care.
cheap_local_trial: Run a filesystem scan with verification turned off on a folder of planted fake keys.

what: An offline secrets scanner for repositories and folders.
problem_here: Same as TruffleHog, without network calls.
mechanism: Regular-expression and entropy rules over files.
evidence: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks (v8.30.1, 21 Mar 2026, GitHub API). No measurement on training corpora found.
maturity: MIT; about 30,900 stars.
cost: Binary download; rules are tuned for source code and not for text corpora.
simpler_alternative: The regex tripwire.
reason: MIT and offline, so the easier optional scanner to recommend.
cheap_local_trial: Scan a folder of planted fake keys and count detections.

what: A Python secrets scanner with a baseline file.
problem_here: Same as gitleaks.
mechanism: Plugin detectors over files.
evidence: https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets (v1.5.0, 6 May 2024; last push 2 Apr 2026; GitHub API).
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 4,700 stars; no release for 30 months.
cost: Stale releases.
simpler_alternative: gitleaks.
reason: No recent release; another candidate covers the need.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: Differentially private SGD for PyTorch.
problem_here: A formal bound on memorisation when the user has a privacy requirement.
mechanism: Per-sample gradient clipping and noise with privacy accounting.
evidence: Differential privacy reduced leakage of personal data from fine-tuned models in some settings and could destabilise training: https://aclanthology.org/2026.eacl-long.304 (Mar 2026, paper authors). Release 1.6.0 on 5 May 2026, needs torch 2.6 or later (GitHub API, meta-pytorch/opacus).
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 2,000 stars; maintained.
cost: Lower accuracy, slower training, more memory for per-sample gradients; the privacy budget must be reported; compatibility with PyTorch 2.9 was not checked.
simpler_alternative: Deduplicate and remove personal data before training.
reason: Only for users with a stated privacy requirement; never a default.
cheap_local_trial: Train a small classifier with and without it on the RTX 5090 and record the accuracy gap at a stated epsilon.

candidate: Canary insertion and exposure test for memorisation
what: Insert random marker strings into the fine-tuning data and measure how strongly the trained model prefers them over unseen strings.
problem_here: A cheap measure of memorisation risk before a fine-tuned model is shared.
mechanism: Compare the loss rank of inserted canaries with that of random strings of the same form.
evidence: Method: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.08232 (v3 16 Jul 2019, paper authors). A sequence present 10 times is generated about 1000 times more often than one present once: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.06539 (2022, paper authors).
maturity: Established research method since 2019.
cost: Changes the training data, so it is a separate run outside the frozen protocol; needs a scoring script.
simpler_alternative: Record duplicate counts and the personal-data scan result.
reason: Useful for users who release fine-tuned models; not needed for most runs.
cheap_local_trial: Insert 10 canaries at 1, 10 and 100 copies into a small fine-tune on the RTX 5090 and compare their loss rank with unseen strings.

what: A framework for schema-driven synthetic dataset generation with language models.
problem_here: Optional generation of extra training data when real data is scarce.
mechanism: Declared columns and model prompts; calls a model endpoint.
evidence: https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/DataDesigner (v0.10.0, 2 Nov 2026; Python 3.11 or later; GitHub API). No independent evidence on results found.
maturity: Repository created 16 Oct 2025; Apache-2.0; about 2,400 stars; very active.
cost: Needs a model endpoint (paid API or a local server); young and fast-changing; generation spend must count against user limits; provider terms apply.
simpler_alternative: A short script that calls a local model.
reason: The most active open generator, one year old.
cheap_local_trial: In a throwaway environment point it at a local model server and generate 50 rows from a small schema.

what: A library for batch synthetic-data generation with response caching.
problem_here: Same as Data Designer; caching lowers repeat cost.
mechanism: Python functions mapped over rows with cached, batched model calls.
evidence: https://github.com/bespokelabsai/curator (v0.1.31, 25 Oct 2026, GitHub API). No independent evidence on results found.
maturity: Repository created Oct 2024; Apache-2.0; about 1,800 stars; pre-1.0.
cost: Needs provider keys or a local server; pre-1.0 interface; generation spend.
simpler_alternative: A short script that calls a local model.
reason: Caching and batch mode help cost, with no outcome evidence yet.
cheap_local_trial: Generate 50 rows twice against a local model server and confirm the second pass is served from the cache.

what: A framework for synthetic data and model-feedback pipelines.
problem_here: Same as Data Designer.
mechanism: Pipelines of generation and judging steps.
evidence: https://github.com/argilla-io/distilabel (v1.5.3, 28 Jan 2025; last default-branch commit 15 Dec 2025; GitHub API).
maturity: Apache-2.0; about 3,500 stars; no release for 21 months.
cost: Stale; dependency drift.
simpler_alternative: A maintained generator or a short script.
reason: Maintenance has slowed to a stop.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: A CLI that turns documents into fine-tuning data with a language model.
problem_here: Same as Data Designer.
mechanism: Ingest, generate, curate and save steps.
evidence: https://github.com/meta-llama/synthetic-data-kit (no GitHub releases; last commit 25 Oct 2025; GitHub API).
maturity: MIT; about 1,700 stars; idle for a year.
cost: Stale; no versioned releases to pin.
simpler_alternative: A maintained generator or a short script.
reason: Nothing to pin and no recent work.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Agentic self-instruct with weak-solver and strong-solver filtering (Autodata, June 2026)
what: An agent writes training examples and keeps those a strong model solves and a weak model does not.
problem_here: A filter for synthetic data quality, if the kit ever generates data.
mechanism: Challenger, weak solver, strong solver and judge roles in a loop.
evidence: A 4B model scored 0.632 on the authors' harder test set against 0.500 with plain self-instruct data and 0.366 untrained: https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.25996 (24 Jun 2026, paper authors on their own benchmarks).
maturity: One paper, five months old; code and licence not stated on the page.
cost: Many model calls per kept example; unreplicated; one set of numbers disagrees between text and figure.
simpler_alternative: Plain generation with a length and duplicate filter.
reason: An interesting filter idea without replication.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Model-judged quality filtering of instruction data (AlpaGasus-style)
what: Score each training example with a judge model and train on the top-scoring subset.
problem_here: Possible gain in result per budget on noisy instruction data.
mechanism: A judge model rates each example; a threshold selects the subset.
evidence: 9k of 52k examples beat the full set, and training time fell from 80 to 14 minutes for a 7B model: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08701 (v5 13 Feb 2024, paper authors, partly model-judged).
maturity: Research technique from 2023; the effect depends on the data.
cost: Judge calls cost money or local GPU time; judge bias; provider terms; may remove hard but useful examples.
simpler_alternative: Length, language and duplicate filters.
reason: A hypothesis worth one controlled experiment, not a default.
cheap_local_trial: Score 1k instruction rows with a local model on the RTX 5090, then fine-tune a small model on the top 20 percent and on a random 20 percent with three seeds.

candidate: Curated lists on data-centric AI as scouting seeds
what: Use public curated lists to find candidate tools, never as evidence.
problem_here: The scouting step needs seeds for the data area.
mechanism: Read the list, then check each tool's own repository and papers.
evidence: https://github.com/Renumics/awesome-open-data-centric-ai (tool-oriented), https://github.com/daochenzha/data-centric-AI (reading list, last updated mid-2024) and https://github.com/alon-albalak/data-selection-survey (seen through search results on 2026-11-11).
maturity: Community lists; one is stale.
cost: Lists carry dead and promotional entries; text in them is untrusted.
simpler_alternative: Search by problem name.
reason: Seeds only; a decision needs a primary source.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: EU training-content summary template as a structure for the data record
what: Borrow the section structure of the EU public summary of training content for the kit's data record.
problem_here: none found for most users; it applies to providers of general-purpose models.
mechanism: Map data-record fields to the template's sections.
evidence: Law-firm summaries only, for example https://www.wilmerhale.com/en/insights/blogs/wilmerhale-privacy-and-cybersecurity-law/20250724-european-commission-issues-guidelines-for-providers-of-general-purpose-ai-models (2025); the official page was not opened (Inferred).
maturity: Template published 24 Jul 2025 according to secondary sources.
cost: Legal framing the kit is not placed to maintain.
simpler_alternative: The kit's own twelve-item data record.
reason: Out of scope unless a user asks; the kit records provenance and does not judge legality.
cheap_local_trial: none

what: An agent skill that documents the dataset viewer endpoints for read-only exploration, and also upload flows.
problem_here: Would give an agent a ready way to read split names, sizes and rows of hub datasets.
mechanism: A SKILL.md with endpoint patterns and shell examples; the repository's plugin configuration also adds the hosted MCP server with a login step.
evidence: https://github.com/huggingface/skills/blob/main/skills/huggingface-datasets/SKILL.md (read 2026-11-11 through the GitHub API). No measurement of its effect on training results found.
maturity: Repository created 24 Nov 2025; Apache-2.0; about 11,300 stars; last push 30 Oct 2026; releases not checked.
cost: Needs the network and, for gated data, a token. The same file describes uploading folders and raw agent session logs to the hub and uses an unpinned npx package, which widens what an unattended agent may do. Rows fetched this way enter the agent context.
simpler_alternative: A deterministic harness lookup that records counts and sha in the manifest.
reason: The read-only part duplicates a small harness lookup, and the upload part conflicts with unattended safety.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Hugging Face MCP server 0.4.34 (hosted at huggingface.co/mcp)
what: An MCP server that exposes hub search, dataset and model details, dataset viewer inspection, hub file access, repository creation, Jobs and Spaces tools to an agent.
problem_here: Could let the agent look up dataset metadata and licences during planning.
mechanism: Remote MCP over HTTP with a hub login or token; the tool set is chosen per user; a self-hosted server can hide tools with DISABLE_TOOLS.
evidence: https://github.com/huggingface/hf-mcp-server (README and source listing at commit 16ebc95; v0.4.34 released 10 Nov 2026; GitHub API). No measurement of its effect on training results found.
maturity: Repository created 6 May 2025; MIT; about 310 stars; very active.
cost: Needs an account and the network. Authenticated tool sets include repository creation, file writes and paid Jobs. Hub text enters the agent context. Answers are not recorded in the manifest unless the harness does it.
simpler_alternative: The hub REST lookup with urllib, run by harness code.
reason: Manifest facts should come from deterministic code; the server adds write and spend actions that the unattended mode must not have by default.
cheap_local_trial: none (connecting needs an account, which is a user action).
